newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm oil to benefit from Pakistan import duty cut.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil to benefit from Pakistan import duty cut.

text.p: The Malaysian palm oil market is expected to rally further if Pakistan confirmed a cut in its import duty on edible oils, traders said on Monday.
A Pakistani dealer said at the weekend the government planned to cut the duty by 1,000 rupees per tonne.

"The market has already reacted to the Pakistan rumour this morning," a trader with a commission house said. "If the cut is confirmed, we will see vegetable oils, including palm oil, gain further ground."
The trader added: "A cut will mean that it is much cheaper for Pakistan to buy oil."
Official figures showed Pakistan bought 917,138 tonnes in the first nine months of 1996, against 804,860 tonnes in the same period in 1995.
At midday, benchmark third position Malaysian palm oil futures contract was up seven ringgit at 1,271 ringgit a tonne.
